claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Pulumi programs can reference existing Terraform state files.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
The Pulumi Terraform provider exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` objects provide a `getOutput(name)` method for reading Terraform outputs.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves outputs from another Pulumi stack.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties (where logging can be "DEFAULT").
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
The `pulumi import` command takes the form `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
There is a 'Pulumi import API' usable programmatically to import resources.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, with policies having `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel` and `validateResource` fields; `enforcementLevel` accepts "mandatory".
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
Automation API embeds Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` and provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` with `stackName`, `projectName`, `program`, plus `stack.setConfig` and `stack.up({ onOutput })` returning `outputs`.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team rather than development teams.
The `@pulumi/terraform` package exists and exports `terraform.state.S3Reference`.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and use `registerOutputs`.
